steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease and flour 24 3-inch madeleine molds.
Beat eggs, vanilla, and lemon zest in a medium bowl with an electric mixer on high speed for 5 minutes. Gradually beat in confectioners' sugar. Beat for 5 to 7 minutes or until thick and satiny.

Sift together flour and baking powder. Sift 1/4 of the flour mixture over the egg mixture, gently fold in. Fold in the remaining flour by fourths. Then fold in the melted and cooled butter. Spoon batter into the prepared molds, filling 3/4 full.

Bake in the preheated oven until the edges are golden and the tops spring back, 10 to 12 minutes. Cool in molds on a rack for 1 minute. Loosen cookies with a knife. Invert cookies onto a rack and cool.
Sift confectioners' sugar over the tops or melt semi-sweet chocolate chips and dip the tips in the chocolate. Store in an airtight container.

raw_recipe.headline: Madeleines
raw_recipe.description: This madeleine recipe makes the greatest afternoon tea cookie. You can sprinkle the top with sugar or dip the tips in chocolate. Easy and delicious.

review.reviewBody: This recipe turned out perfect for me! The cookies are light and sweet the perfect compliment to coffee or tea. Some people had difficulty getting them out of the pan and my advice would be to use shortening (like crisco) to grease the pan and then dust well with flour. Make sure your eggs are room temperature when you start and not right out of the fridge our they will grow and froth up too much. Other hints... oh i tapped the pan on the counter instead of using a knife to loosten and they just fell right out. Good luck!

Loved them! I had never made these before. I ordered the special pans ( absolutely worth the money). I might not have been so eager to try them if I had a hand held mixer! My KitchenAid made it so easy! The step by step instructions and the video helped me to do them correctly. This recipe made 22 Madeleines. Melting the butter ahead then letting it cool while I mixed worked perfectly. Carefully folding in the flour/baking powder then folding in the cooled butter made them so light. Melt in your mouth. I used a pastry brush and brushed melted butter into the “cups”. I didn’t use any flour. When they were done, I turned the pans over and they FELL out! I sprinkled sugar on some, left some plain and dipped some in melted chocolate. The only problem We ate them too fast to take pictures If you take care and follow the instructions you and you’re family will be enjoying them with coffee! Allrecipes is my go to for new recipes and, as always, they didn’t disappoint! Thank you for another perfect recipe!

My suggestions: I spray my mold with 'butter'-flavored spray and they fall out instantly. Wipe off excess spray and batter from around molds. I use a mini madeline sheet and get 36 smaller bite-sized cookies - bakes for only half of time (5-6 mins) in two batches. Can use any type of citrus zest or as other have done vary the extract flavoring. These are a great Go-To Cookie - so simple.

I followed this recipe exactly. My husband is in love with these cookies or cakes, depending on how you see them. They are so delicious. Very light, great with coffee. I’ll make them again. I put my dough in the refrigerator for an hour before baking, they baked up nice and tall. Crispy on the edges and light in the middle. So good. You definitely need a Madeline pan to bake them in. I bought mine on amazon for under 12 dollars.

Used vanilla and almond and left out the lemon zest. Only needed to spray the pan with vegetable spray for the first batch only. Let cool for 1 minute, then removed. Immediately made the second batch in the same pan while it was still hot. My family actually liked the second batch better. I needed to bake both batches for closer to 13 minutes.

Overall the Madeline's tasted good. I made two batches. The second one I ended up baking them at 325 instead of what the recipe called for- 375. When I did bake them at 375 they were to crispy on the outside and not cooked in the middle. They basically sucked. I loved the flavor even after I added extra lemon zest and vanilla extract. A note for others who want to make this is to make sure the oven is not to hot and the Madeline's don't get too overbaked. Overall the cookies were okay.
Use the USA Pan madeleine pan and they will slide right out even while still warm. This recipe works even though I used a manual mixer and didn't quite cool the butter.

These are wonderful and so easy to make! I agree with another reviewer that the baking temp is a bit to high...I tried it at 350 and they came out perfect! I made a batch with raspberry extract and they were a big hit at my tea party! Also, for those who had trouble with their pans...the nonstick madeleine pans are a breeze to use and not expensive. I used a fork to immediately remove to wire rack with no problem. This recipe is a keeper!
This was fabulous. I added some almond extract and decreased the temp of the oven to 325 degrees. I poured the mixture into a ziplock bag and used it to pipe the mixture into the pans. Loved it.

I love this recipe because I think using confectioner's sugar gives the cookies better texture than regular white sugar. I used Pam for baking on the cookie sheets and they lifted off perfectly. I followed the recipe, although it only made 21 instead of 24.
Also, I didn't use lemon zest. Instead I used 1 teaspoon almond extract and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract to give them a stronger flavor. And you don't have to beat the eggs for 5 whole minutes. I only beat them on high for 3 and my cookies turned out great. Delicious and easy to make!
Used orange zest and 2tbs Cointreau instead of lemon mmmmmmm

Made these tonight with the kids and they are all gone. They were delicious, perfect flavor and texture. Used unsalted butter to grease the pan and sifted the flour for both the batter and the pan. Followed recipe exactly - thanks for the wonderful recipe.

The ladies were impressed, which was what I was going for. Made exactly one dozen. I didn't have a lemon for zest, so I tried a tsp of lemon juice which couldn't be detected. Next time I might be nice to try almond extract if I don't have lemon. These were moist and delicious even if they weren't lemony. Took the full 12 minutes to get a brown edge. With olive oil and flour these fell right out of the pan. Dusted them with powdered sugar while they were still hot and the sugar disappeared. Will wait for them to cool next time. One large Madeleine was enough. If I make them in the morning, I'll have time to dip them in chocolate. Thanks for the recipe! Instructions were easy and they turned out so nice.
Need to know not to make mixture to think at all. But more practice the better I get I suppose. Which there was a video how to make it.
A sweet treat, made even better if dipped in chocolate.
I made these instead of pancakes for breakfast. They turned out lovely. Did them in muffin pans as I don't have a proper madeleine pan.
i made these and they turned out chewy and gross. a lot of them didnt come out of the tray and the ones that did didn't look nice.
My kids loved them! Light and fluffy. I used silicone molds with spray and flour - came right out!

I LOVE this recipe....I love lemon so I add 1/2 t lemon extract in addition to vanilla (and 2 T lemon jus). I found 2 black nonstick madeleine pans which I lightly coat with butter and the cookies slide off after 1 min. cooling. I can't keep the cookie tin full....they keep disappearing!
Great!
